title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's People Operations (People Ops) guidance for: hiring practices, candidate experience, new hire onboarding, 30-60-90 plans, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers running direct reports.

Please use the checklists, scorecards, and templates in the appendices when making role decisions, running interviews, or supporting new hires.

1) Hiring: principles and process

Intro
- Goal: hire diverse, high-performing teammates with excellent role fit while minimizing time-to-offer and candidate drop-off.
- Principles: structured interviews, calibrated scorecards, inclusive sourcing, clear candidate communications, and compliance with legal/EEO policies.

Stage-by-stage process (standard flow)
1. Requisition & role scoping
   - Owner: hiring manager + people-ops partner.
   - Deliverables: job spec draft, interview rubric, target compensation band, diversity sourcing plan.
2. Sourcing & screening
   - Recruiter screens resume and does 20–30 min screen.
   - Record screening notes in ATS and share top-of-funnel metrics weekly.
3. Interview loop
   - Structured 3–5 stage loop depending on level: take-home (if used), technical interview(s), cross-functional interview, hiring manager interview, and final leadership check for senior hires.
   - Use standardized scorecard for each stage (see Appendix A).
4. Calibration & decision
   - Interviewers submit scorecards before the debrief. Debrief meeting chaired by hiring manager and attended by recruiter and people-ops. Decision requires consensus and documented risk areas.
5. Offer & negotiation
   - Offer prepared by recruiter using approved comp band and pre-configured template. People-ops signs off on equity/comp exceptions.
6. Background checks & references
   - Initiated after verbal offer acceptance. Standard checks: identity, employment verification, and any role-required checks (e.g., export control, security clearance).
7. Acceptance & hand-off to onboarding
   - Recruiter and hiring manager coordinate start date, preboarding tasks, equipment request, and first-week schedule.

Interview best practices
- Use objective, behaviorally-anchored rubrics. Score each dimension 1–5 with observable evidence.
- Avoid disallowed topics (age, medical, marital status, religion).
- At least one interviewer trained in inclusive interviewing should be present for every final-stage interview.
- Provide interview feedback within 48 hours. If a candidate is rejected, send a respectful closing note within 72 hours.

Time-to-hire SLAs (guideline)
- Requisition posted -> first on-site/loop scheduled: 7 business days.
- First interview -> decision: 10 business days.
- Offer -> acceptance: 7 business days.

2) Candidate experience & communications

Key commitments to candidates
- Transparent timeline at first contact.
- Clear interview agendas and preparation materials.
- Prompt communication on status and decision rationale where appropriate.

Email templates (examples)
- Screening invite: short agenda + interviewer names + calendar links.
- Rejection note: thank you + brief reason + suggested resources for reapply timeline.

3) Onboarding: pre-boarding through first 90 days

Onboarding goals
- Clear expectations, role context, relationships established, tools access, and early impact plan.

Pre-boarding checklist (to complete before start date)
- Offer letter signed and returned.
- Equipment order placed: laptop, monitors, peripherals.
- Account creation: SSO, corporate email, Slack, VPN, Atlassian Confluence, Jira, GitHub access request submitted.
- New hire packet sent: org chart, team README, first-week agenda, code of conduct, benefits summary.

First day checklist
- 09:00 Welcome (People Ops) — orientation and benefits overview.
- 10:00 Manager 1:1 — role intro, expectations, immediate first-week tasks.
- 11:30 Lunch with buddy — informal intro.
- 13:30 IT walk-through — confirm access to required systems.
- 15:00 Team onboarding meeting — introductions and team rituals.

30-60-90 template (Manager and new hire use jointly)
- 30 days (observe & learn): complete environment setup, complete required trainings, pair with peer/buddy, deliver first small task.
- 60 days (contribute): own recurring tasks, complete cross-team meetings, identify first project to lead.
- 90 days (impact): lead a project milestone, present learnings and next-quarter goals.

Onboarding roles and responsibilities
- Hiring manager: first-week plan, 30-60-90 goals, weekly 1:1s.
- People Ops: orientation, benefits enrollment, policy review.
- IT/Facilities: equipment and access provisioning.
- Buddy: day-to-day team culture questions and informal help.

4) Performance cycles & feedback

Cycle cadence
- Annual performance cycle with two half-year checkpoints (mid-cycle review) and quarterly check-ins recommended for fast-moving teams.

Expectations and artifacts
- Goals (OKRs): set at org and team level; role-level objectives should map to team OKRs.
- SMART objectives recommended for performance goals.
- Performance reviews combine: manager assessment, self-review, peer feedback.

Review timeline (example)
- Goal-setting window: first two weeks of quarter.
- Quarterly check-ins: manager + direct report documented in Confluence notes.
- Mid-cycle review: narrative update + calibration meeting for leveling/promo considerations.
- Annual review: summary, compensation/bonus recommendations.

Feedback best practices
- Continuous feedback model: encourage timely feedback via 1:1s and peer notes.
- Use balanced feedback: specific behavior, impact, and suggested next steps.
- Document informal coaching conversations and follow up in next 1:1.

Performance rating guide (manager rubric excerpt)
| Rating | Description | Manager actions |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| Exceeds Expectations | Consistently delivers above scope; leadership or exceptional ownership | Consider stretch roles, promo conversation |
| Meets Expectations | Delivers to scope with a few growth areas | Continue development plan and regular coaching |
| Needs Improvement | Below expectations on core responsibilities | Create performance improvement plan (PIP) if no improvement in 30–60 days |

Calibration and fairness
- Calibration sessions led by people-ops to review manager ratings and ensure consistency across teams. Use anonymized evidence where possible.
- Managers must provide written examples supporting ratings.

5) Manager guide: hiring, onboarding, and development responsibilities

Hiring responsibilities
- Draft clear role spec + success criteria.
- Build a diverse interview panel.
- Ensure interviewers complete training on structured interviewing.
- Close loop with candidate: timeline, decision rationale, and timely communication.

Onboarding & early development
- Set the 30-60-90 plan jointly during the first week.
- Run weekly 1:1s for the first 12 weeks; then move to a cadence that fits the team.
- Assign a buddy and define expected buddy interactions.

Performance management & growth
- Provide ongoing coaching with documented outcomes.
- Hold regular career conversations at least twice a year.
- Advocate for strong performers during calibration cycles.

Handling low performance
1. Informal coaching: immediate manager-led coaching with clear expectations and success measures. Document conversation.
2. Formal performance plan: if no measurable improvement in 30–60 days, work with people-ops to create a PIP with defined milestones and check-ins.
3. HR escalation: if PIP fails or if there are conduct issues, escalate to people-ops for next steps.

Legal & compliance notes
- Ensure interview questions avoid protected characteristics. All hiring documentation must be stored in the ATS.
- For roles with export-control or background screening requirements, follow the security-and-compliance guidance and secure approvals before offer.

6) Templates & appendices

Appendix A — Interview scorecard (example fields to copy into ATS or Confluence)
- Candidate name: 
- Role: 
- Interviewer: 
- Date: 
- Dimensions (scale 1–5): Role knowledge/technical, problem solving, communication, culture fit, hiring bar (yes/no)
- Evidence notes: (short, concrete examples)
- Recommendation: Strong hire | Hire | No hire | Needs more info

Appendix B — New hire checklist (copyable)
- Pre-start: offer signed, equipment ordered, accounts requested, new-hire packet sent.
- Day 1: orientation, manager 1:1, buddy lunch, IT access validated.
- Week 1: complete onboarding trainings, shadowing sessions, first task.
- Week 4: 30-day check-in documented.
- Week 8: 60-day feedback and adjustment.
- Week 12: 90-day performance checkpoint and goal reset.

Appendix C — Example 1:1 agenda (recommended short form)
- Quick personal check-in (5 minutes)
- Wins since last 1:1 (5 minutes)
- Blockers and help needed (10 minutes)
- Career/development topic (10 minutes)
- Action items and commitments (5 minutes)

Appendix D — Common forms & links
- Job requisition template: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/job-requisition-template
- ATS candidate workflow and pipeline: see recruiter playbook (internal)
- PIP template and legal guidance: /confluence/policies-and-process/pip-template

7) FAQs and troubleshooting

Q: Who decides final hire?
A: The hiring manager is the decision owner; people-ops signs off on process fidelity and comp approvals.

Q: What if an interview panel is missing a domain expert?
A: Do not skip domain validation. Schedule an additional short technical validation step or include a recorded take-home exercise with rubric.

Q: How do I escalate urgent access problems for a new hire starting tomorrow?
A: Contact IT via #it-help (Slack) and people-ops oncall; use the emergency onboarding runbook.

Document governance
- People Ops maintains this page. Managers should review it annually and submit update requests via the people-ops doc request form.
- Significant process changes require cross-functional review (legal, finance, security) and a published change log.
